ActionResult.description:
What the four `/api/*` levers answer: task cancel and dismiss, MCP
reconnect and disconnect, a rewind, a compaction.

`ok` is whether the thing was done, not whether the request was
understood — a request that was not understood is a 400 with a reason and
never reaches this shape.

message.description: What to show the person who asked.

prefillPrompt.description:
A rewind hands back the prompt of the turn it rewound to, so the
composer can be refilled with it. Absent on every other lever, and on
a rewind the owner performed.

turns.description:
How many turns the rewound conversation has left. Absent for the
same reason.

background.description: Whether it runs in the background by default.

description.description: When to use it, from the definition's own words.

effort.description: The reasoning effort it pins, or `null`.

model.description: The model it pins, or `null` to follow the session's.

name.description: The agent type, which is what a spawn names.

tools.description: The tools it is allowed, or `null` for the default set.

id.description: The value to set the agent config option to.

label.description: What to show in the picker.

agents.description: Every agent definition this server can run.

AnswerQuestionsParams.description:
[`method::ANSWER_QUESTIONS`]: the answer to an AskUserQuestion.

Its own method rather than the standard permission answer because
AskUserQuestion is several questions with several selected options each,
and the standard result carries one option id.

turnGeneration.description:
Fences the answer against the turn that asked. Defaulted for the wire
so a peer from before this field reads as turn zero, which is what it
always meant.

AssistantContentBlock.description:
A single content block inside an assistant message. Dispatched
by the `type` discriminant.

The deferred variants (`server_tool_use`, `advisor_tool_result`,
`connector_text`, plus any future Anthropic content block
variants) fall through to [`AssistantContentBlock::Other`] via
`#[serde(other)]`, preserving the raw JSON so legacy rows don't
break parsing.

AssistantGeneratedImageBlock.description:
`{ type: 'generated_image', id, status?, revised_prompt?, media_type,
data, saved_path? }` — the assistant-side image payload produced by
the OpenAI Responses `image_generation` built-in tool. Kept aligned
with `rebon_api::GeneratedImageBlock` so transcripts round-trip.

Rebon no longer requests that tool (image generation is the `ImageGen`
tool now); the block stays so transcripts written before still render.
`data` is optional because the engine of that time stripped the base64
payload once it had saved the image, leaving `saved_path` as the
load-bearing field — the renderer surfaces that and the revised prompt.

AssistantMessage.description:
One assistant row as persisted in a transcript line.

Only the fields the renderer reads are modelled; the engine-side
bookkeeping (`requestId`, `apiError`, `error`, `errorDetails`,
`isVirtual`, `usage`, `message.id`, `message.model`,
`message.stop_reason`, `message.container`,
`message.context_management`) is not duplicated here — it will
land as part of the engine bridge.

advisorModel.description:
`advisorModel` — threaded to advisor rows. Advisor blocks
are not rendered yet but the field is preserved so round-trip
stays lossless.

isApiErrorMessage.description:
`isApiErrorMessage` — keeps API error rows visible even in
brief-only mode.

isStreamContinuation.description:
`Some(true)` on a row minted when the inline overflow flush split
one still-streaming text block across scrollback commits. The
renderer joins such a row to the previous one — no leading margin,
no gutter dot — so the split halves read as a single message.

AssistantMessageInner.description: The `message` sub-object on an assistant row.

role.description:
Tolerated when absent, for the same reason as
[`UserMessageInner::role`].

AssistantRedactedThinkingBlock.description:
`{ type: 'redacted_thinking', data: '...' }` — the renderer shows
a `[redacted thinking]` placeholder and never reveals `data`.

AssistantThinkingBlock.description:
`{ type: 'thinking', thinking: '...' }` — note the inner field is
`thinking`, not `text`, per the Anthropic SDK schema.

AssistantToolUseBlock.description:
`{ type: 'tool_use', id, name, input }`. The `input` is opaque
Anthropic-SDK JSON — this code doesn't introspect it; per-tool
rendering lands in future renderer extensions.

raw_output.description:
Raw tool output payload, retained in-memory so rewind can
restore file contents for the current session.

Also on the wire, and not redundant with `tool_call_content`:
`enrich_tool_use_blocks` leaves that `None` for a result with no
structured update content, and this is then the only carrier of
the output a card has to show.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status. Set live during a turn and on replay
from the matching `tool_result`; serialized when present so a
card off the wire can tell a completed call from a failed one.

tool_call_content.description:
Tool call content payloads (e.g. `Diff` for Edit tools).

Populated from the streaming overlay when the tool completes, and
on replay by [`crate::transcript_replay::enrich_tool_use_blocks`]
from the matching `tool_result`. Serialized when present so a
surface reading rows off the wire sees the tool output the
terminal sees; absent when there is none, so a row that was never
enriched serializes to exactly the bytes it did before.

AttachmentRow.description:
`{ type: 'attachment', attachment: ... }` row wrapper. The inner
`attachment` payload is kept as opaque JSON: the rich typed attachment
shape lives with the engine, and keeping it opaque here avoids
cross-crate type bleed.

AuthMethod.description:
One way to authenticate with an agent, as advertised in
`initialize`.

The spec's shape is `{ id, name, description? }`. Every field is
optional here and unknown keys are kept, on purpose: nothing in
Rebon reads this yet, and an agent that grows a field would
otherwise fail the *whole* handshake over a value nobody looked at.
A real agent already broke this once — `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`
sends `{id, name, description, _meta}`, and requiring a `type` field
that the spec never had made `initialize` undecodable.

AutoModeAllowSource.description:
Which part of the auto-mode gate let a tool call run without a dialog.

Display-only, and worth distinguishing because the three are not the same
event: a classifier verdict is the machine's judgement, a cached verdict is
that judgement replayed, and an exemption is the *user's* own approval — a
row that says "auto mode allowed this" over an approval the user gave by
hand misattributes it.

oneOf.description: A fresh classifier verdict cleared the call.
A classifier verdict remembered from an identical earlier call.
The user approved this call themselves (a `/permissions` retry).

Source not recorded — a transcript or a peer written before the
source was carried. Renders as the original unattributed note.

CancelCallParams.description:
[`method::CANCEL_CALL`].

Not a cancel of the *turn*: that is `session/cancel`. This releases one
call, because a client timeout that only drops its own receiver leaves the
owner working on something nobody will read.

CancelCallResult.description:
Whether a waiter was actually let go.

Always an ok answer: cancelling a call that is not running is not a
failure, it is "nothing to release" — which is what a client that raced its
own timeout needs to hear.

ClientLease.description: One client holding a session open.

ClientLeaseKind.description:
Which surface a lease belongs to. Carried so `rebon agents` and the Agent
View can say *who* is holding a session open rather than only that someone
is.

DiffContent.description:
Diff content payload — `oldText` may be `null` (when the file did not
exist). `old_text` is optional, so the wire form `"oldText": null`
round-trips faithfully.

FilesResponse.description: `GET /api/files` — the file picker's candidates for one workspace.

files.description: The candidates, a directory marked by a trailing slash.

problem.description: Why the directory could not be listed. Absent when it could.

root.description: The directory the paths are relative to.

scanning.description:
Whether the workspace index is still being built, so an empty list
means "not yet" rather than "nothing".

truncated.description: Whether more matched than were returned.

ForegroundQuestion.description: One interactive question (AskUserQuestion), mirrored for the controller.

ForegroundQuestionAnswer.description:
The controller's answer to one interactive question: chosen option indices
plus optional free-form text. With no selected option the text is an Other
answer; with selected options it is supplemental notes.

ForegroundQuestionOption.description:
One option of an interactive question, mirrored from the engine's
`AskUserQuestionOption` so the controller can render it.

GapParams.description:
[`method::GAP`]: the owner dropped deltas from its ring.

What is missing between `from` and `to` is in the events file, which is the
authority; the client reads it from there and resumes. A gap is never an
error — an owner that outran a slow client is doing the right thing.

HelloParams.description: [`method::HELLO`], the first message on a new subscription.

cursor.description: Where the stream is resuming from.

epoch.description:
The owner's numbering. It restarts each time an owner starts, so a
cursor alone cannot be compared with one written by its predecessor.

HistorySnapshot.description: `GET /api/history` — a session as the page reopens it.

messages.description:
**Deprecated.** The model's view of the
session, folded a second and different way: it carries tools meant
for their own surface, and it deletes a whole user block where the
row stream keeps the half a person typed. Nothing first-party reads
it; `rows` is what the terminal, the page and the desktop app show.

rows.description: The display rows the terminal draws, from the one producer.

title.description: Its title, or `null` for one that has none.

_meta.description:
Top-level extension data — a sibling of `agentCapabilities`,
not inside it. This is where the steering wire protocol
advertises itself: both `claude-agent-acp` and `codex-acp` put
`{"steering": {"supported": true}}` here. `default` keeps
agents without it decodable, which is also the compatibility
story: no `_meta`, no steering, fall back to queueing.

KernelLoopOption.description: One kernel loop vendor, and whether this session could switch to it.

backendId.description: The backend name a switch would name.

bundled.description:
Whether this build carries the vendor's assembly. A known but
unbundled vendor keeps its seat so the switch can say so loudly
instead of "no such vendor".

configured.description: Whether a provider and model are configured for it.

id.description: The vendor id: the `/kernel` argument and the config key.

switchable.description: Whether the router has this backend to switch to.

LeaseParams.description: [`method::LEASE`]. While any lease is live the owner stays up.

error.description: The warning naming this server, if one does.

name.description: The name it is configured or connected under.

tools.description: The tool names it contributes, prefixed. Empty unless connected.

transport.description:
`stdio`, `http` or `sse`; `null` for a server that only the client
knows about, which is how an env-declared one arrives.

McpServerSnapshot.description: One MCP server the owner has configured, as the owner sees it.

source.description:
Where the entry came from: the project's `.mcp.json`, the CLI, a
plugin.

McpStatus.description: `GET /api/mcp` — the MCP servers this process configured and connected.

problem.description: Why the configuration could not be read at all.

servers.description: One per server, configured or merely connected.

warnings.description:
Per-server warnings the loader collected.

The server has always sent these; declaring them here changes no
bytes and lets the page read them without a cast.

McpStatusSnapshot.description:
The owner's MCP servers, for a client that hosts none of its own.

Names and states only, never a tool's schema: this rides on every
`status` event, and a client shows it rather than calling anything
through it.

McpToolSnapshot.description: One tool the owner's MCP servers offer the model.

name.description: The `mcp__<server>__<tool>` name the model calls it by.

tokens.description: What its definition costs the context, approximately.

ModelsResponse.description: `GET /api/models` — what this session can be switched to.

models.description:
Every model the provider offers, the current one first if it is not
among them.

provider.description: The active custom provider, or the runtime's own provider name.

OutOfRangeRuntime.description: A Node that answered, but not with a version this build accepts.

PermissionOption.description: One option offered to the client when the agent asks for permission.

PluginEntry.description:
One entry of the composition, and whether it loaded.

A projection of the server's own `ComposeEntry`, not that type: the entry
carries a dozen more fields — config, seats, topics, command names — and
this listing shows seven of them.

loaded.description: Whether this entry is in the running plane's loaded set.

PluginPlaneStatus.description: The running plane, or the reasons there is none.

generation.description: Which generation it is, or `null` when nothing is running.

problem.description: Why the composition could not be read at all.

refusal.description: Why the composition was refused, in the refusal's own words.

running.description: Whether a plane is up in this process.

PluginRuntimeStatus.description: The Node runtime under a plugin plane.

configuredPlugins.description:
How many entries `kernelPlugins` asks for. Zero is a normal state,
not a problem — the section is opt-in.

A count, not a boolean: nothing on the page ever read it as a flag.

installable.description: Whether `rebon node install` could fix this here.

outOfRange.description:
A Node that was found and turned down for its version.

Separate from `problem` because it is a different situation with a
different fix.

problem.description: The resolver's own words for why nothing resolved.

resolved.description: The runtime that resolved, or `null` if none did.

supported.description: The versions a runtime may report, as a range someone can read.

PluginStatus.description:
`GET /api/plugins` — the plugin plane as this process sees it.

The page's answer to "is my plugin running": what runtime it would run on,
what the composition asked for, what loaded, and why the rest did not.

entries.description: One per leaf the composition resolved, in load order.

host.description: Which loop host this build carries, in one line.

loops.description: The kernel loop vendors a session can be switched to.

plane.description: The plane that is actually up, if one is.

runtime.description: The Node runtime a composition would run on.

skipped.description:
Entries that could not be turned into a load request, and why.

A plugin that starts and is then refused at every registration is a
worse failure than one that never starts, so each line carries its
reason rather than only a name.

RebonMeta.description:
What rebon hangs at `_meta.rebon` on standard ACP messages.

The standard shapes are fixed, and several rebon facts have to ride along
anyway: which cursor a `session/update` carries, which pending permission a
`session/request_permission` is about, the fence a `session/cancel` is only
valid against. ACP reserves `_meta` for exactly this, so nothing standard
is bent to fit.

Every field is optional and skipped when absent, so a message that needs
one fact does not carry the other nine as nulls.

commandId.description:
Makes a retry idempotent: the owner answers a repeat of the same id
from its recent-results memory instead of running the command twice.

cursor.description:
Where in the owner's numbering a `session/update` sits.

In `_meta` rather than in the standard params because the client's
de-duplication reads it (`crate::client::stream_watermark`) and the
standard shape has nowhere to put it.

epoch.description:
Which numbering that cursor belongs to. An owner's cursors restart when
it does, so a cursor from a previous epoch is not comparable with this
one and must not be used to skip anything.

extraText.description:
Free-form text alongside a permission answer.

The standard result carries an option id and an updated input and has
nowhere for this, and it is not decoration: with no option selected it
*is* the answer.

fence.description:
What a `session/cancel` is only valid against.

Standard `session/cancel` is a bare notification, which is fine when a
client and an agent share one process and cannot disagree about what is
running. Across a socket they can, so the cancel says which turn it
meant and the owner drops it if that is no longer the turn in flight.

jobId.description:
The job this addresses. A fence, not a routing key: a worker that has
been replaced must not act on a command meant for its predecessor.

queryId.description:
Which pending permission a `session/request_permission` is about.

Carried because the owner re-sends still-pending permissions to a
client that attached after they were raised, so the answer is merged by
this id rather than by which connection it arrived on.

token.description:
The token a client presents on `initialize`. Checked once, when the
connection is established, because the connection is what it
authenticates.

turnGeneration.description:
The turn a permission, an answer or a cancel belongs to, so a stale one
is refused rather than applied to whatever is running now.

deliberate.description:
Whether the user meant to be done, as opposed to merely detaching.

Only decides how long the owner lingers, and only when this was the
last lease. Defaulted for the wire: a client from before this field
reads as `false`, which is what every release did until it existed.

executable.description:
Where it lives, as a string: the server has a path and the wire has
no path type.

origin.description:
Which rung of the ladder answered: an explicit demand, a managed
install, or `PATH`.

complete.description: Whether the turn finished. An unfinished one is still a checkpoint.

index.description: The turn number, counting from the start of the session.

preview.description:
The first 240 characters of the prompt, with an ellipsis when it was
cut.

timestamp.description: When it was sent, or `null` on a turn whose line carried no stamp.

uuid.description: The user message this turn began with.

RewindResponse.description: `GET /api/rewind` — where a session can be rewound to.

filesSupported.description:
Whether it can restore files too, which needs the session's host —
the file-history snapshots are the host's.

problem.description: Why files cannot be restored, or `null` when they can.

supported.description: Whether this server can rewind a conversation at all.

oneOf.description: The transcript only; files on disk are left alone.
The files only, from the file-history snapshot.
Both, refused up front unless the code half can be applied cleanly.

output.description:
Absent for a command that ran and printed nothing. A command that
*failed* is a JSON-RPC error instead, so this is never an error channel.

ServerInfo.description: `GET /api/info` — what this server is and what it is running.

activeTurns.description: Sessions with a `session/prompt` in flight on the server right now.

agentConfigOption.description: The config option id that selects an agent.

agents.description: The agents the page may switch between.

cwd.description: The directory the server was started in.

initialize.description:
The handshake the mux completed, or `null` before it has.

The mux keeps it as the JSON it received, so that is what is passed
on. An [`InitializeResult`] in every case that matters, and the page
reads it as one; typing it here would mean a decode and a re-encode
on a value nothing in this process looks at, and a field the agent
added would be dropped on the way through.

model.description: The model id the runtime resolves to.

provider.description: The provider the runtime model resolves to.

steering.description: Whether this server accepts steering mid-turn.

webUi.description: Where the page's assets came from, for the footer.

SessionExtAck.description: A method that answers nothing but "done".

SessionExtNoParams.description:
A method that takes nothing: [`method::PING`], [`method::STATUS`],
[`method::RECONCILE_PLUGINS`].

A struct rather than `null` so adding a field later is not a wire break: an
old peer sending `{}` still decodes, and a new peer's extra key is ignored
rather than refused.

SessionStatusSnapshot.description:
Everything a client must agree with the owner about (invariant I4).

The client keeps no authoritative copy of any of it: a permission mode, a
model, or a busy flag that a client believes and the owner does not is the
bug class this whole snapshot exists to remove.

busy.description: A model turn is in flight, so a client shows Stop rather than Send.

lastCommandId.description:
The `command_id` most recently processed, and how it went. A client that
lost its connection mid-command reads the outcome here instead of
guessing whether to retry.

mcp.description:
The owner's MCP servers. `None` from an owner that hosts none, or one
from before this field existed.

turnGeneration.description: Fences every answer and cancel against the turn it was meant for.

oneOf.description: Streaming text content from the model.

User input that was queued while a prompt was already running and then
consumed between tool rounds.
Streaming extended-thinking delta.
End of thinking stream for the current turn.
Initial tool-call announcement.
Follow-up tool-call status/content transitions.

A tool call cleared rebon's auto-mode gate without a permission
dialog.

Purely an annotation for the tool row that is already on screen: it
carries no content, and clients must not fold it into anything the
model reads back.

source.description:
Defaulted so a peer that predates the field still decodes — it
lands as `Unspecified` and renders the unattributed note.

oneOf.description: Context compaction has started.
Context compaction finished.
Plan entries.
Slash commands list.
Config option update.

Session-local context was reset and the engine is continuing
with a fresh conversation (e.g. approved clear-context plan).
`plan` carries the plan text so the client can render it as a
system message in the cleared transcript — without it the user
sees a blank screen even though the model is executing the plan.
Session info update (title, timestamp).

Token usage reported by the model during streaming.
Emitted as snapshots arrive from the provider or as the engine
approximates streamed output so the client can display progress.

SessionUsageSnapshot.description: Token spend for the session, as the status bars show it.

SetOptionParams.description:
[`method::SET_OPTION`].

Separate from running the slash command a human would type, because a
client that wants to *set* a value should not have to compose that command
and the owner should not have to parse it back.

description.description: One line about what it does.

hint.description: What its argument looks like, or `null`.

name.description: The skill's id, which is also how it is invoked.

path.description: The directory it was loaded from, or `null` for one that has none.

userInvocable.description: Whether it appears in the `/` menu.

skills.description: Every skill the registry knows, enabled or not.

oneOf.description: Built-in CLI command (help, clear, compact, ...).
User/bundled skill (/simplify, /commit, ...).
Agent-related command (/agent, /agents, /teams, ...).

SteeringOutcome.description: What became of a steering request.

oneOf.description: Delivered into the running turn.

The turn raced ahead and finished; the agent started a fresh
turn with the message instead. Fire-and-forget on the agent's
side — the new turn's output flows through `session/update`
with nobody awaiting a prompt response.

since.description:
Resume from just after this cursor. Absent means "from wherever the
owner's ring starts", and the [`method::HELLO`] that follows says where
that turned out to be.

SystemMessage.description:
`{ type: 'system', subtype, level, content, ... }`.

Subtype-specific payloads (API error, file snapshot, compact boundary,
local command, …) exist on the wire but are not typed here.
This type only exposes the common fields the renderer reads:
`subtype`, `content`, `level`, `isMeta`. The rest stay on the wire
as extra JSON fields — they're not dropped, they just aren't
surfaced as typed fields here.

content.description:
Present on most typed subtypes; optional so legacy rows
don't fail to parse.

backgrounded.description: Whether it was sent to the background.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601, or `null` on a task with no start time.

id.description: The task id, which is what an action names.

kind.description: What kind of task it is.

output.description: Its result as text, or `null` while it runs.

TasksResponse.description: `GET /api/tasks` — the background tasks of one session.

TerminalContent.description: Terminal handle reference inside a tool-call content payload.

ToolCallContent.description: Content payload attached to a tool-call update — discriminated by `type`.

ToolCallLocation.description: File-system anchor that a tool call references.

ToolCallReference.description: Reference to the tool call a permission request is gating.

ToolKind.description: Tool kind enum used by `tool_call` updates.

ToolResultContent.description: Union of the two valid shapes for a tool_result `content` field.

TranscriptRow.description:
Single transcript row type matched by the Rust renderer.

`#[serde(tag = "type")]` maps directly to the wire `type` field —
so `{"type":"user", ...}` deserializes as `Message::User(_)`
for each row in a JSONL transcript file.

oneOf.description:
`type: 'attachment'` row. Kept as opaque JSON; the richer variant
modelling lives with the engine's own attachment message type and is
not modelled here.

Open-world fallback — any top-level `type` value not listed
above (including `grouped_tool_use` / `collapsed_read_search`,
plus legacy `progress` rows
bridged from legacy data). The raw JSON is preserved byte-for-byte
so round-trips are lossless.

stopReason.description:
Why a turn ended. Absent on the one that started, and on an end whose
reason the owner does not have.

stopRefused.description:
Why a cancel did not stop this turn.

The turn is still running when this is set -- `state` says so. It is
here rather than in the answer to whoever asked, because every client
watching is looking at a turn that did not stop.

TurnStreamState.description: Whether a turn is in flight.

UsageResponse.description: `GET /api/usage` — the token ledger for one session.

cacheCreationTokens.description: Cache writes, on the same terms.

cacheReadTokens.description:
Cache reads, which only the session's own host counts. `null`
without one.

durationMs.description:
How long the session has been open, or `null` for one this server
did not open.

inputTokens.description: Tokens sent, including the turn in flight.

messages.description: Messages on disk, or `null` when the transcript could not be read.

model.description: The model the runtime resolves to.

outputTokens.description: Tokens received, including the turn in flight.

problem.description:
Which of the two counts this is, in words, because the difference
matters to whoever reads the number.

turns.description: How many turns the ledger has seen.

UserContentBlock.description:
A single content block inside a user message. Dispatched by
the `type` discriminant: `text`, `image` or `tool_result`.

UserImageBlock.description:
`{ type: 'image', source: { ... } }` content block. The source
shape is Anthropic-SDK defined and not consumed by the renderer
directly here — preserved as opaque JSON so wire
round-trip is lossless.

UserMessage.description:
Normalized user message fields consumed by the Rust renderer.

* `uuid`, `timestamp` — row identity.
* `message.content` — the Anthropic content block array.
* `isCompactSummary` — branch to compact-summary rendering.
* `isMeta`, `isVisibleInTranscriptOnly` — filter hints used by
  user-message visibility and sticky-prompt handling.
* `imagePasteIds` — paste ids for `<image>` blocks.
* `planContent` — optional plan override path.

UserMessageInner.description:
The `message` sub-object on a user row. Matches the shape that the
Anthropic SDK's `MessageParam` wraps — a `role: 'user'` string and
a `content` array.

role.description:
Absent on a hand-authored or older line; a row that says nothing
about its role is the role its parent row already declared, and
dropping it whole would lose a message a person really sent.

UserRole.description:
The `role` literal on a user message. Always `"user"` on the
wire; modelled as a single-variant enum so deserialization
rejects a *wrong* role instead of silently accepting it as `Other`.
A *missing* one is tolerated — see [`UserMessageInner::role`].

UserToolResultBlock.description:
`{ type: 'tool_result', tool_use_id, content, is_error? }`.

`content` on the wire can be a string OR an array of content
blocks (Anthropic's nested content format). This implementation
accepts both via an untagged helper: strings become
`ToolResultContent::Text(_)`, arrays become
`ToolResultContent::Blocks(_)`. The renderer currently only
formats the string form; the Blocks form falls through to a
JSON-stringify display.

WebUiSource.description:
Where the page's own files came from.

The two cases are not the same shape and never have been: an embedded
build reports the commit it was built from and a null path, and a
directory reports its path and no `built` key at all. Kept asymmetric on
purpose — adding `"built": null` to the directory case would be a change
to the wire.

built.description: What the embedded build was built from. Absent for a directory.

path.description: The directory being served, or `null` when embedded.

description: Generated by `cargo run -p rebon-schema-gen` from crates/rebon-proto, crates/rebon-types and crates/rebon-session-host. Do not edit by hand.
title: rebon ACP wire types
